rv.q: Having seen many versions of Three Sisters over the years to varying degrees of success, I cannot emphasise how well-crafted this production is, how it adeptly captures the essence of the play while also proving so enjoyable to watch.
It’s a production that skilfully draws out the play’s combination of wit, absurdity and humanity.
Steinbeis’ bold staging pushes the possibilities of the intimate space, playing with the light in satisfyingly surprising ways.
Caroline Steinbeis’s bewitchingly tender and amusing tender production starts and ends as brightly lit as I’ve seen this venue.
Steinbeis’s direction struggles to direct our attention, with the momentum coming far more in the text than the action.
Caroline Steinbeis’ production finds laughter in even the most unexpected places.

cn.t: Critics praise this candlelit Sam Wanamaker Playhouse production for its intimate atmosphere and Rory Mullarkey's fresh translation, with Steinbeis's direction drawing out Chekhov's dark humor with confidence and clarity.
